evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Blanca Calvo Figueras and colleagues
evidence_items.locator: Section 5, discussion paragraph beginning Larger models are more truthful
evidence_items.explanation: The study finds better truthfulness in larger same-family models. It also identifies post-training alignment as a possible contributor and limits generalization beyond TruthfulQA, so it does not demonstrate a scale-only solution.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Ihsan A. Qazi and colleagues
evidence_items.locator: Section 2.2, Conversational versus specialized prompting effects on multilingual LLM fact verification
evidence_items.explanation: The evaluation supplies material evidence of better fact-checking performance in larger models across multilingual claims. Differences in model families, prompting and abstention prevent attribution to scale alone or a conclusion that the problem is solved.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Matthew R. DeVerna and colleagues
evidence_items.explanation: The study reports continuing political fact-checking weaknesses across 15 models and stronger results with curated context. These finite results are consistent with Marcus's concern but cannot establish that future scaling will never solve it.

evidence_items.publisher: Association for Computational Linguistics; author version hosted on arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: ReFACT reports persistent error-localization failures across tested scales from 1B to 70B parameters. This is evidence of a remaining limitation in scientific factuality, not a general impossibility result for all future scales.
